classification.habit: Perennial rhizomatous herb, 60–90 cm tall, with large leaves arising in a tuft.
classification.habitat: Warm humid tropical regions on well-drained loamy soils; grown as a field crop.
classification.distribution: Extensively cultivated in all parts of India, notably Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Odisha and Maharashtra.

identification.description: Primary ovate or secondary cylindrical branched rhizomes with deep orange-yellow interior and characteristic aromatic odor.
identification.whole_plant: Stemless herb with tufts of large oblong leaves and a short pseudostem arising from a branched aromatic rhizome.
identification.root: Fibrous roots arise from the rhizome, some ending in small tubers.
identification.stem: Underground rhizome ovate, oblong or cylindrical and branched, externally yellowish-brown with annulations and root scars; fracture horny, orange to reddish-brown; aerial pseudostem formed by leaf sheaths.
identification.leaf: Large, oblong-lanceolate, 30–45 cm long, long-petioled, with sheathing bases.
identification.flower: Pale yellow flowers in a cylindrical spike with green and pinkish bracts arising from the centre of the leaf tuft.
identification_points: Rhizome with annulations and root scars
Horny fracture, orange to reddish-brown interior
Central cylinder about twice as broad as cortex
Characteristic aromatic odour and bitter-pungent taste

therapeutics.precautions: May add to anticoagulant and antiplatelet effects; high doses may cause gastric irritation. Use cautiously in gallstones and biliary obstruction.
therapeutics.contraindications: Avoid large medicinal doses in pregnancy, biliary obstruction and before surgery; culinary use is safe.

वर्ण्या त्वग्दोषमेहास्रशोथपाण्डुव्रणापहा ॥१९७॥

modern_information.evidence_summary: Turmeric is powerful anti-inflammatory and detoxifying herb.
modern_information.safety_notes: Safe as a spice; concentrated curcumin products have been linked to rare liver injury and can interact with anticoagulants.
